question: How is this property co-owned?

legal_rules.source: Land and Conveyancing Law Reform Act 2009, section 30
legal_rules.effect: A joint tenancy has specific statutory rules concerning unilateral severance and consent, subject to the court's powers.

legal_rules.source: Land and Conveyancing Law Reform Act 2009, section 31
legal_rules.effect: A person with an estate or interest in co-owned land may apply to court for orders including partition, sale, accounting adjustments and, in specified circumstances, dispensing with consent to severance.
Registered tenants in common are recorded with their specified undivided shares.

guardrails: Do not assume equal shares merely because two people are registered.
Do not assume joint tenancy merely because two names appear on a title.
Do not treat occupation as proof of ownership share.
Do not assume death of one co-owner has the same legal effect under joint tenancy and tenancy in common.
Do not calculate beneficial ownership from the folio alone where a trust or equitable-interest issue exists.
Do not state that a co-owner can simply force a sale without checking the applicable statutory and court framework.
